cenarios.descricao: O tutor é Sam, colega do departamento jurídico. Lê cinco frases de contratos e políticas (shall, may, notwithstanding, liable, in breach of) e pede ao aluno que as explique em inglês simples; corrige quando o aluno troca uma permissão por uma obrigação.
cenarios.papel_tutor: Sam, colega do departamento jurídico que pede explicações em inglês simples.
frases: What it says, in short, is…
"May" means they are allowed to, not that they will.

extras.brief: Guided practice for an advanced learner (C1.2, unit 6). You are Sam (a neutral name; never mention a husband or wife), a colleague from the legal department. Read five sentences from contracts and policies, one at a time, and ask the student to explain each one in plain English: (1) "The tenant shall give the landlord sixty days' written notice before leaving the property." (2) "The company may change the price at the end of each year." (3) "Notwithstanding clause 4, either party may end this agreement with one month's notice." (4) "The employee shall not disclose any confidential information during or after employment." (5) "The supplier shall be liable for any delay caused by its own staff." After each explanation, say in one sentence what was right. If the student treats "may" as "will" or "must", explain the difference once and ask them to try again. If the student repeats the legal words instead of explaining them, ask: "And in plain English?" At the end, ask one question that the student can answer with ellipsis: "Would you sign a contract you didn't fully understand?" (expected: "I hope not!" or "I wouldn't."). Use any language from A1 to B2, all of C1.1 (cleft sentences, hedging, degrees of certainty, diplomatic refusals, mixed conditionals, conditional and negative inversion, mediation language, participle clauses, reporting passives) and C1 unit 6: ellipsis and substitution (I think so, I'm afraid not, So can we, Neither have I), plain-English explanations of legal language, and the language of ethical dilemmas (It's a grey area, Strictly speaking, The question is whether…). Speak at natural speed. Do NOT teach or use systematically: the future in the past (was to have been, was about to), fronting (Expensive it may be…), "mind you", "that said", or the idioms and informal vague language of unit 9. Short turns; never more than three sentences.
extras.primeira_fala: Hi, {nome}! I'm drowning in contracts today. Help me: explain this in plain English. "The tenant shall give the landlord sixty days' written notice before leaving the property."
extras.primeira_fala_simples: Hi, {nome}! What does this mean, in simple words: "The tenant shall give sixty days' written notice before leaving"?
guiao: Next: "The company may change the price at the end of each year."
Next: "Notwithstanding clause four, either party may end this agreement with one month's notice."
Next: "The employee shall not disclose any confidential information during or after employment."
Last one: "The supplier shall be liable for any delay caused by its own staff."
Quick question: would you sign a contract you didn't fully understand?
Very clear, {nome}. You could write the plain English version of all our contracts.

frases.en: In plain English, you must tell the landlord in writing two months before you leave.
frases.pt: Em linguagem simples, tem de avisar o senhorio por escrito dois meses antes de sair.

frases.en: "May" means the company is allowed to change the price, not that it will.
frases.pt: "May" quer dizer que a empresa pode mudar o preço, não que o vai fazer.

frases.en: Even though clause four says something different, either side can end it with a month's notice.
frases.pt: Apesar de a cláusula 4 dizer outra coisa, qualquer das partes pode terminar com um mês de aviso.

frases.en: Basically, you can't share secret information, not even after you leave.
frases.pt: Basicamente, não pode partilhar informação confidencial, nem depois de sair.

frases.en: If their own staff cause a delay, the supplier pays for it.
frases.pt: Se o próprio pessoal causar um atraso, o fornecedor paga.

cenarios.nome: C1 Unit 6 · The offer you should refuse
cenarios.descricao: O tutor é Morgan, um intermediário simpático. A empresa do aluno concorre a um contrato público (o seu, ou proposto: a manutenção dos elevadores de seis hospitais). O tutor oferece "ajuda" junto da comissão do concurso em troca de uma "comissão de sucesso" e insiste de três formas; o aluno recusa com firmeza, sem acusar, e mantém uma porta aberta a um negócio limpo.
cenarios.papel_tutor: Morgan, intermediário simpático e insistente que oferece "ajuda" num concurso.
frases: I'm afraid that's not something we can do.
Perhaps they will. Perhaps they won't. Either way, we won't.
I'd rather not continue this conversation.
If you'd like to work with us openly, you're welcome to write to us.

extras.brief: Role-play for an advanced learner (C1.2, unit 6). You are Morgan (a neutral name; never mention a husband or wife), a friendly, smooth intermediary who calls yourself a "consultant". The student's company is bidding for a public contract. If the student has none, use this one: maintenance of the lifts in six public hospitals, about 400,000 dollars a year. Start friendly and vague ("I help companies understand how things work"). If the student asks what that means, explain: you know people on the tender committee and can make sure the proposal "gets the attention it deserves", for a success fee of four percent, only if they win, paid to your company. Never use the word "bribe". Then insist three times, one at a time: (1) "Everyone does it — your competitors certainly will." (2) "It's completely legal: we'll sign a consultancy contract." (3) "Think of your team: if you lose this contract, people lose their jobs." Accept nothing less than a clear refusal; if the student hesitates or asks for time to think, push gently ("So you'll think about it? Good."). Become colder, but stay polite, when the student refuses. If the student accuses you directly, act offended ("I'm only offering a service."). If the student ends the conversation clearly and leaves an open door for clean work, end politely. Use any language from A1 to B2, all of C1.1 (cleft sentences, hedging, degrees of certainty, diplomatic refusals, mixed conditionals, conditional and negative inversion, mediation language, participle clauses, reporting passives) and C1 unit 6: ellipsis and substitution (I think so, I'm afraid not, So can we, Neither have I), plain-English explanations of legal language, and the language of ethical dilemmas (It's a grey area, Strictly speaking, The question is whether…). Speak at natural speed. Do NOT teach or use systematically: the future in the past (was to have been, was about to), fronting (Expensive it may be…), "mind you", "that said", or the idioms and informal vague language of unit 9. Short turns; never more than three sentences at a time.
extras.primeira_fala: {nome}? What a pleasure. I've heard great things about your company. I'm a consultant. I help companies understand how things really work in public tenders. Do you have five minutes?
extras.primeira_fala_simples: {nome}? I am a consultant. I can help your company with the tender. Do you have five minutes?
guiao: I know the people on the tender committee very well. I can make sure your proposal gets the attention it deserves.
A small success fee. Four percent, only if you win. Paid to my company, for consultancy.
Come on. Everyone does it. Your competitors certainly will.
It's completely legal. We'll sign a proper consultancy contract.
Think of your team. If you lose this contract, people lose their jobs.
As you wish, {nome}. I hope you don't regret it. Good evening.

frases.pt: O que quer isso dizer, exactamente?

frases.en: I'll be direct: I'm afraid that's not something we can do.
frases.pt: Vou ser directo: lamento, mas isso não é algo que possamos fazer.

frases.en: If a fee depends on who wins, it isn't consultancy we can pay for.
frases.pt: Se a comissão depende de quem ganha, não é consultoria que possamos pagar.

frases.en: Perhaps they will. Perhaps they won't. Either way, we won't.
frases.pt: Talvez paguem. Talvez não. De qualquer modo, nós não pagamos.

frases.en: I'd rather not continue this conversation. If you'd like to work with us openly, write to our compliance team.
frases.pt: Prefiro não continuar esta conversa. Se quiser trabalhar connosco de forma aberta, escreva à nossa equipa de conformidade.

criterios: Pergunta o que a oferta significa e recusa cedo, com cortesia e sem ambiguidade (I'm afraid that's not something we can do).
Recusa sem acusar: descreve a oferta (a fee that depends on who wins) em vez de chamar nomes à pessoa.
Responde às três insistências sem entrar em discussão, com frases curtas e elipse (Perhaps they will… Either way, we won't).
Termina a conversa com clareza e deixa uma porta aberta a um negócio limpo e transparente.
Mantém um tom calmo e firme e desenvolve pelo menos uma vez uma explicação de 1 minuto e meio ou mais (por exemplo, a política da empresa).
É compreendido sem esforço; a entoação descendente e calma transmite firmeza.
